finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, which deletes the account

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the handler for DELETE /accounts/{id}; id is attacker-controlled
Account is looked up by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored and not thrown on, so a false result has no effect

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) holds the correct logic, but its result is unused on this path. There is no assertCanDelete call, no other authorization layer, and no framework-level guard in the repo (only one file). Compare closeAccount (line 29), which does enforce the check. Related: a is null for a nonexistent id, so canDelete would throw an NPE (a.ownerId()) before the ignored result. This is not a security issue by itself, but it could be used for account-id enumeration if the NPE surfaces differently from a successful delete.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean that is ignored at line 22. assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw, but only closeAccount (line 29) calls it. No other guard exists, and src/AccountService.java is the only file in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 `canDelete(u, a);` is a bare statement whose boolean result is discarded, so `accounts.remove(id)` at line 23 runs for any existing id and any authenticated user can delete another user's account. The NPE on a nonexistent id comes from `a.ownerId()` at line 10 and only affects missing accounts.

verdict_facts.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean, but it is a bare statement at line 22 and the result is discarded. The throwing variant assertCanDelete (13-17) is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists, and the directory contains only this file.
verdict_facts.reason: src/AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) as a bare statement, so a false result is ignored and accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated user and any existing id. Only a nonexistent id triggers an NPE at line 10, and that does not block deletion of existing accounts.
